newsitem.title: POLAND: Kredyt to take 29 pct of Russian bank.
newsitem.headline: Kredyt to take 29 pct of Russian bank.

text.p: Poland's Kredyt Bank SA signed an agreement with Investbank AO, based in Russia's Kaliningrad enclave, under which it would pay $1.15 million for a new share issue representing 29 percent of Investbank's equity, Kredyt's president told a news conference on Monday.
Pacuk said the deal was aimed at tightening cooperation between the two banks in financing and settlements of trade between Poland and the Russian enclave and boosting their share of business.
"We hope that in a short period we will be able to jointly service 50 percent of all trade turnover between Poland and the Kaliningrad region," Pacuk said.
He said that last year's turnover amounted to $126 million in 1995 and in the first 11 months of this year Kredyt Bank had processed $23 million worth of transactions with the Russian enclave.

Pacuk said that if the deal wins a go-ahead Kredyt Bank would become the largest shareholder of Investbank, which now has 2,400 stakeholders with four institutions holding stakes of five percent or more.
Kredyt Bank currently has representative offices in Vilnius and Kaliningrad and holds a 13.3-percent stake in the Kiev International Bank.
It also has Lithuania's central bank permission to establish a branch in the Baltic state.
